# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

This report documents the Stage 1 (Process Design) characterization of the A-Mab
production bioreactor (Step 3), the fed-batch mammalian cell-culture operation that
establishes the N-glycosylation, charge-variant and initial size-variant and
process-impurity profile of the drug substance. The study was executed under the
Process Characterization Plan **PCP-003** on a qualified 2 L scale-down model
(SDM), following the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011; @pdatr60;
@ispegpg2023] and the Quality-by-Design principles of ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11], with the process model, quality-attribute framework and
risk methodology of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

Nine process parameters were evaluated. A `{python} n_scr`-run resolution-V
fractional-factorial screening design identified the significant factors and
two-factor interactions for five cell-culture CQAs; a `{python} n_rsm`-run
face-centred central-composite response-surface design then quantified main
effects, interactions and curvature and defined the multivariate design space. The
response-surface models are adequate for all five CQAs
(R² = `{python} f"{R2_MIN:.2f}"`–`{python} f"{R2_MAX:.2f}"`, adjusted R² ≥
`{python} f"{ADJ_MIN:.2f}"`, predicted R² ≥ `{python} f"{PRED_MIN:.2f}"`) with no
significant lack of fit relative to the center-point pure error.

The production bioreactor is demonstrated to be well understood and robust. The
design space, parameter classifications and proven acceptable ranges support the
Stage 2 operating ranges and the drug-substance control strategy, and this report
rolls up into the Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**).

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose principal mechanism of action
is antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC), with a contributory
complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) component; both are governed by the Fc
N-glycosylation profile [@amab2009]. The production bioreactor is a fed-batch
mammalian cell culture operated at `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L
working volume. It is the only upstream operation that forms product-quality CQAs
and is therefore the sole upstream step used to define the upstream design space;
the seed-expansion and harvest operations influence titer and process consistency
but do not form or modify product-quality attributes [@amab2009]. Product quality
established in the bioreactor — afucosylation, high mannose, galactosylation, acidic
charge variants and aggregate, together with the host-cell protein (HCP) and DNA
impurity load presented to the purification train — is the subject of this
characterization.

## Objectives

The objectives of the study were to (i) establish the quantitative relationships
between the production-bioreactor process parameters and the cell-culture CQAs;
(ii) define the multivariate design space over which all CQAs are met
simultaneously; (iii) establish proven acceptable ranges (PARs) and normal
operating ranges (NORs) for each parameter; (iv) classify each parameter for its
risk of impact to CQAs and to process performance; and (v) provide the process
understanding and ranges that justify the Stage 2 operating conditions and the
control strategy.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The work follows the lifecycle approach to process validation of the FDA 2011
guidance [@fda2011], PDA Technical Report 60 [@pdatr60] and the ISPE Good Practice
Guide [@ispegpg2023], and applies the enhanced (QbD) development approach of ICH Q8,
Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11]. Criticality is treated as a continuum
(ICH Q9). The report structure corresponds to the Stage 1 Process Design Report of
PDA TR 60 §3.11 and provides development-report content suitable to support a
Biologics License Application.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The characterization ranges and set-points are supported by platform knowledge from
related humanized IgG1 antibodies (referred to as X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and by
A-Mab clinical and engineering manufacturing experience [@amab2009]. Prior knowledge
established that Fc glycosylation (afucosylation, high mannose, galactosylation)
governs ADCC/CDC potency and is set in cell culture; that aggregate formed in
culture is subsequently polished downstream; and that the harvest HCP and DNA burden
is generated upstream and cleared by the purification train. This knowledge framed
the CQAs in scope and the prioritization of parameters for characterization.

## Quality attributes affected by the production bioreactor

@tbl-cqa summarizes the CQAs set or principally established by the production
bioreactor, with their acceptance criteria and criticality. Criticality is scored on
the A-Mab continuum using Tool #1 (Risk Score = Impact × Uncertainty); attributes
rated High (H) or Very High (VH) are treated as *Critical* [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
```

: CQAs established by the production bioreactor, with acceptance criteria and criticality (Tool #1 = Impact × Uncertainty; H/VH = Critical). {#tbl-cqa}

The glycosylation attributes are the most critical because they govern potency;
afucosylation and galactosylation are managed within target ranges, whereas high
mannose (Very High criticality) is controlled to a narrow upper limit. Aggregate is
established in culture and polished at cation exchange; acidic charge variants,
HCP and residual DNA are followed here as they load the purification train.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

Consistent with the A-Mab lifecycle of iterative risk assessments, the
characterization scope was set by the Pre-Characterization Process Risk Assessment
(**RA-001**), which used prior knowledge and a risk-ranking-and-filtering screen to
prioritize parameters and to assign the study type. Parameters with a credible
main-effect and interaction risk to the glycan and charge-variant CQAs (culture pH,
temperature, dissolved CO₂, osmolality and culture duration) were assigned to the
multivariate DoE; parameters expected to affect only process performance were
assigned to univariate assessment or held at their set-point [@amab2009; @pdatr60].
The parameters and ranges carried into this study are given in @tbl-param
(§5.1).

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

All characterization runs were performed on a qualified 2 L bench-scale bioreactor
operated at the commercial working-volume equivalent for pH, temperature, dissolved
oxygen and CO₂ control, gas sparging, agitation power per unit volume and feeding
strategy (**SOP-2003**, **SOP-2004**). The SDM was qualified against at-scale
reference data (**SOP-1001**) by comparing both the operational parameters and,
critically, the input and output quality attributes — viable cell density,
viability, titer, and the afucosylation, galactosylation, high-mannose,
charge-variant, aggregate, HCP and DNA profiles — confirming that the model is
representative and suitable to support design-space and PAR claims [@pdatr60]. The
between-run reproducibility of the center-point condition (§6.1) provides a direct,
quantitative estimate of model precision and is used as the pure-error term in the
lack-of-fit assessment of every response-surface model.

## Cell line, media and culture operation

The production culture is a fed-batch process inoculated from the N-1 seed
bioreactor at the target initial viable cell concentration, using platform basal
medium and a bolus nutrient feed (**SOP-2004**). Culture pH, temperature, dissolved
oxygen and dissolved CO₂ are controlled to set-point by the bioreactor control
system; osmolality is a monitored culture attribute governed by the feed and base
addition; and the culture is harvested on the nominal duration criterion. Raw
materials and cell-culture media are controlled to platform specifications and are
treated as identity/quality-controlled inputs rather than characterized variables,
consistent with the A-Mab platform approach [@amab2009].

## Analytical methods

CQAs were measured by validated methods (@tbl-methods). Released N-glycans were
determined by 2-AB HILIC-UPLC (**AMV-3010**); size variants (aggregate/HMW) by
SEC-HPLC (**AMV-3011**); HCP by ELISA (**AMV-3012**); charge variants by imaged
capillary isoelectric focusing (**AMV-3013**); and residual host-cell DNA by qPCR
(**AMV-3014**). Method performance characteristics are summarized in Appendix D.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(amvs=None, sops=[]))
```

: Validated analytical methods used in the characterization. {#tbl-methods}

## Sampling plan

Each DoE run was sampled at harvest for the released CQAs (glycan map, charge
variants, aggregate) and for the harvest HCP and residual-DNA load; daily process
samples (viable cell density, viability, metabolites, pH/pCO₂ verification) were
taken to confirm culture trajectory. Center-point runs were replicated within each
design (three in screening, four in the response-surface design) to quantify
reproducibility and pure error.

## Statistical methods

Designs were constructed and analyzed in coded factors, with each parameter's
characterization range mapped so that the set-point is 0 and the range edges are
±1 (**SOP-1002**). Screening data were analyzed by ordinary-least-squares regression
of each response on the main effects and all two-factor interactions; factor
*effects* are reported as twice the coded coefficient. Response-surface data were
analyzed with the full quadratic model (main effects, two-factor interactions and
pure-quadratic terms). Statistical significance was assessed at α = 0.05. Model
adequacy was judged by the coefficient of determination (R²), the adjusted R², the
predicted R² (computed from the PRESS statistic by leave-one-out), the overall model
F-test, and an analysis of variance partitioning the residual into lack of fit and
pure error, the latter estimated from the replicated center points; a
non-significant lack-of-fit F-test (p > 0.05) indicates an adequate model. The
design space was defined as the multivariate region of the four dominant factors
over which every CQA response satisfies its acceptance criterion simultaneously.
Commercial-scale process capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches with each parameter varied within its
NOR, reporting the process-capability index (Cpk) one-sided for impurity CQAs and
two-sided for target-range CQAs.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

Nine parameters were studied (@tbl-param). The characterization range of each
multivariate factor ("PAR" column) defines the edges of the explored knowledge space
and the basis of the proven acceptable range; the NOR is the tighter range at which
the parameter is controlled routinely. The DoE factor coding is given in
@tbl-legend.

```{python}

```

: Production-bioreactor process parameters, set-points, ranges and post-characterization classification. {#tbl-param}

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
```

: Design-of-experiments factor legend (coded A–E). {#tbl-legend}

## Screening design

Factor screening used a resolution-V two-level fractional factorial in the five
multivariate factors (A–E) with three center-point replicates,
`{python} n_scr` runs in total. At resolution V, main effects are unconfounded with
one another and with two-factor interactions, so both can be estimated cleanly. The
five responses recorded for each run were afucosylation, galactosylation, high
mannose, acidic charge variants and aggregate. The complete coded design matrix and
run responses are given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The four factors carried forward from screening (culture pH, temperature, culture
duration and dissolved CO₂ — codes A, B, E, C) were studied in a face-centred
central-composite design (cube points, axial points at the face centres, and four
center-point replicates), `{python} n_rsm` runs in total, enabling estimation of
curvature in addition to main effects and interactions. The complete coded design
matrix and responses are given in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

Initial viable cell concentration was evaluated one factor at a time across its
characterization range for its effect on peak viable cell density, titer and culture
trajectory; it was not carried into the multivariate design because prior knowledge
indicated no credible CQA impact.

## Mechanistic interpretation

The response-surface models reproduce the established physiology of fed-batch IgG1
culture. Lower culture pH and lower temperature increase specific productivity,
extend the productive culture and raise titer, with a modest increase in
afucosylation and a decrease in galactosylation. Extended culture duration lowers
both afucosylation and galactosylation and raises the harvest HCP and DNA load as
viability declines late in culture. Dissolved CO₂ and osmolality modulate
galactosylation and the charge-variant profile. The significant culture
pH × duration and pH × CO₂ interactions mean the glycan responses depend on the
*combination* of set-points, which is why a multivariate design space — rather than
independent one-dimensional ranges — is required to assure quality.

# Design space

The design space is the multivariate region of culture pH, temperature, culture
duration and dissolved CO₂ over which all five cell-culture CQAs simultaneously meet
their acceptance criteria, computed by overlaying the individual CQA constraints on
the fitted response-surface models. @fig-ds shows the pH × culture-duration plane at
the set-points of the remaining factors: the shaded region satisfies every CQA at
once, with the afucosylation contours overlaid and the NOR and set-point indicated.
The NOR of each parameter (@tbl-param) lies well inside the design space, which in
turn lies within the broader characterized knowledge space; movement within the
design space is not a change, whereas movement outside it would require assessment
under the quality system [@amab2009; @ichq8].

![Production-bioreactor design space (culture pH × culture duration); the shaded region satisfies all cell-culture CQAs simultaneously, with afucosylation (%) contours overlaid.](../outputs/figures/fig_bioreactor_designspace.png){#fig-ds width=85%}

# Process capability and robustness

A Monte-Carlo simulation of `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` commercial-scale
batches, with every parameter varied within its NOR, was used to estimate the
commercial-scale CQA distributions and process capability (@tbl-cap). Capability is
evaluated one-sided for impurity CQAs (upper limit) and two-sided for target-range
CQAs.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(BR_CQAS), floatfmt=".2f")
```

: Commercial-scale process capability for the bioreactor-set CQAs. {#tbl-cap}

All bioreactor-set CQAs meet their acceptance criteria with margin; the minimum
capability is **Cpk = `{python} f"{min_cpk_br:.2f}"`**, driven by high mannose, which
is the Very-High-criticality attribute held to the narrowest target range. The
capability margin confirms that the NOR-bounded process reliably delivers in-
specification drug substance at commercial scale.

# Parameter classification

Each parameter was classified on the A-Mab continuum from the demonstrated effects
and the design-space risk (@tbl-class). The rationale is as follows.

- **Culture pH, temperature, dissolved CO₂, osmolality, culture duration —
  WC-CPP.** Each significantly affects one or more glycan and/or charge-variant CQAs
  (§6.2–6.3), and several participate in significant interactions. They are, however,
  reliably held within the design space by closed-loop control and continuous
  in-process monitoring, giving a low risk of leaving the design space; they are
  therefore well-controlled CPPs rather than CPPs.
- **Dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration, nutrient feed-1 volume —
  KPP.** These affect peak viable cell density, titer and culture consistency but do
  not significantly impact the CQAs; they are controlled for process performance.
- **Basal medium concentration — GPP.** No meaningful impact on CQAs or performance
  was observed over the wide range studied.


: Post-characterization parameter classification. {#tbl-class}

# Contribution to the control strategy

The production bioreactor is the primary control point for the glycosylation CQAs
(afucosylation, high mannose, galactosylation) and for the acidic charge-variant
profile, and it sets the initial aggregate and the HCP/DNA load presented
downstream. Its contribution to the overall control strategy comprises: control of
the five WC-CPPs to their NORs within the established design space; in-process
monitoring of pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen and pCO₂; harvest on the qualified
duration criterion; released glycan-map, charge-variant, aggregate and HCP testing;
and the trending of the harvest impurity load. The glycan CQAs are controlled
predominantly here because they are not modified downstream, whereas aggregate and
HCP established here are further controlled by cation exchange and by the Protein A /
CEX / AEX train respectively (reported in the paired unit-operation reports and
consolidated in **PCMR-001**).

# Discussion

The characterization quantifies the parameter–CQA relationships for the production
bioreactor, defines a robust multivariate design space, and classifies every
parameter with a data-supported rationale. The response-surface models are adequate
and predictive, and their behaviour is consistent with established fed-batch IgG1
physiology and with the A-Mab prior knowledge, increasing confidence that the SDM is
representative of commercial scale. The principal limitation is inherent to
scale-down characterization: absolute values and the harvest impurity load may shift
modestly at scale, which is why the design space is defined on the qualified SDM and
confirmed at commercial scale during Stage 2, and why the WC-CPP ranges are carried
forward with in-process monitoring. The characterization did not identify any
parameter requiring the most stringent (CPP, as opposed to WC-CPP) control within the
studied ranges.

# Conclusions

The A-Mab production bioreactor is well understood and robust. The relationships
between the culture parameters and the glycan, charge-variant and aggregate CQAs are
quantified by DoE; a multivariate design space is established; every parameter range
is justified by data; and all CQAs meet acceptance at commercial scale with a minimum
capability of Cpk = `{python} f"{min_cpk_br:.2f}"`. The design space, parameter
classifications and proven acceptable ranges provide the basis for the Stage 2
operating ranges and the drug-substance control strategy. This report rolls up into
the Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**) and provides the parameter
risk basis for the post-characterization process risk assessment.

# Deviations from the plan {.unnumbered}

No deviations from **PCP-003** were recorded. All planned runs were executed and all
planned responses were measured on the qualified scale-down model.
